consumer_health_data.note: No consumer health data law or comprehensive privacy law is in force. HB 3494 was re-referred to House Rules on 2026-04-17. SB 2875 was re-referred to Senate Assignments on 2026-05-22.

crossCheck.note: Own search: HB 3494 sits in House Rules and SB 2875 in Senate Assignments. Neither is a Public Act. The Genetic Information Privacy Act covers genetic data only, so it does not set D1.

freeCopyCases: One complete copy free to support a claim for federal veterans' disability benefits
One complete copy free to support a claim for Social Security or SSI benefits
One complete copy free to support a claim for Aid to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled benefits
Updated records free for the same purposes
No handling fee for a patient or personal representative obtaining copies under Section 8-2001.5
feeRules: not to exceed a $20 handling charge for processing the request and the actual postage or shipping charge, if any
for paper copies 75 cents per page for the first through 25th pages
50 cents per page for pages 26 to 50, 25 cents per page above 50, electronic copies at 50% of the paper rate, rates adjusted under Section 8-2006

provisions.title: Examination of health care records, free copy for benefits claims
provisions.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of the law, a health care facility or health care practitioner shall provide without charge one complete copy of a patient's records if the records are being requested by the patient
provisions.appliesTo: Health care facilities and health care practitioners. Free copy only when records support a veterans' disability, Social Security or SSI, or Aid to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled claim.

provisions.title: Examination of health care records, deadline
provisions.quote: The requirements of this Section shall be satisfied within 30 days of the receipt of a written request
provisions.appliesTo: Health care facilities and health care practitioners. Extension allowed to no later than 60 days with a written statement of reasons.

provisions.title: Examination of health care records, fees
provisions.quote: The handling fee shall not be collected from the patient or the patient's personal representative who obtains copies of records under Section 8-2001.5.
provisions.appliesTo: Health care facilities and health care practitioners

provisions.title: Examination of health care records, text after amendment by P.A. 104-598
provisions.quote: Aid to the Aged, Blind, or Persons with Disabilities benefits
provisions.appliesTo: Health care facilities and health care practitioners

copy_rights.note: Free copy for benefits claims goes beyond HIPAA and Part 171. Deadline is 30 days, not shorter. P.A. 104-598, effective 2027-01-01, only renames one benefit program in subsection (h).

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: a free paper copy for benefits claims goes past HIPAA and Part 171. Deadline is 30 days. Minor: the (d-5) handling fee waiver is a fee rule, not a free copy case.

hie_consent.designatedHie: None. The Illinois Health Information Exchange and Technology Act (20 ILCS 3860) is listed as repealed by P.A. 103-508.

provisions.title: Medical Patient Rights Act, HIE opt-out

provisions.appliesTo: Patient information transmitted to or through a health information exchange

provisions.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, HIE opt-out notice
provisions.quote: These rules, standards, or contractual obligations shall provide for written notice of a recipient's right to opt out which directs the recipient to a health information exchange website
provisions.appliesTo: Participants of any HIE. Does not apply to point-to-point transmission directed by the data custodian.

provisions.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, use and disclosure to an HIE
provisions.quote: may, without a recipient's consent, use or disclose information from a recipient's record in connection with an HIE
provisions.appliesTo: Mental health and developmental disability records

crossCheck.note: Statute sets opt-out. HIV and genetic records use the same opt-out route (410 ILCS 50/3). P.A. 104-471, effective 2027-07-01, is correctly listed as pending.

provisions.title: Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, disclosure and consent
provisions.quote: records and communications may be disclosed to someone other than those persons listed in Section 4 of this Act only with the written consent of those persons who are entitled to inspect and copy a recipient's record pursuant to Section 4 of this Act.
provisions.appliesTo: Records and communications of recipients of mental health or developmental disabilities services, subject to Sections 6 through 12.2

mental_health.note: Written consent with listed elements is required for disclosure, with exceptions in Sections 6 through 12.2.

crossCheck.note: 740 ILCS 110/5, current text from P.A. 104-270, effective 2025-08-15. Quote and date match the page.

provisions.title: AIDS Confidentiality Act, disclosure
provisions.quote: No person may disclose or be compelled to disclose HIV-related information, except to the following persons:
provisions.appliesTo: Any person holding HIV-related information

hiv.note: Disclosure of HIV-related information is limited to listed persons.

crossCheck.note: 410 ILCS 305/9, current text from P.A. 102-168, effective 2021-07-27. Quote and date match the page.

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act, confidentiality
provisions.quote: genetic testing and information derived from genetic testing is confidential and privileged and may be released only to the individual tested and to persons specifically authorized, in writing in accordance with Section 30, by that individual to receive the information.
provisions.appliesTo: Genetic testing and information derived from it

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act, confidentiality, text after amendment by P.A. 104-642
provisions.quote: biomarker testing, information derived from biomarker testing, genetic testing, and information derived from genetic testing are confidential and privileged
provisions.appliesTo: Adds biomarker testing and information derived from it

genetic.note: Release only to the person tested or persons they authorize in writing. P.A. 104-642 adds biomarker testing from 2027-01-01.

crossCheck.note: Text before P.A. 104-642 is in force from P.A. 95-927, effective 2009-01-01. P.A. 104-642 adds biomarker testing from 2027-01-01, so pending true is right.

facts.statutoryDamages: Genetic Information Privacy Act: $2,500 negligent or $15,000 intentional or reckless per violation, or actual damages if greater. AIDS Confidentiality Act: $2,000 negligent or $10,000 intentional or reckless per violation, or actual damages if greater.

provisions.title: Genetic Information Privacy Act, right of action
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this Act shall have a right of action in a State circuit court or as a supplemental claim in a federal district court against an offending party.
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of the Genetic Information Privacy Act

provisions.title: AIDS Confidentiality Act, right of action
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this Act or of a regulation promulgated hereunder shall have a right of action in the circuit court
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of the AIDS Confidentiality Act

provisions.title: Reproductive Health Records Privacy Act, violations (right to sue electronic health networks)
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this Act by an electronic health network may bring an action against that electronic health network.
provisions.appliesTo: Electronic health networks; the Act bars actions against health care providers

private_right.note: Rights to sue exist for genetic and HIV records. 740 ILCS 110/15 also lets a person sue for mental health records; its page gives no effective date. No general medical records right found.

crossCheck.note: Rights to sue cover genetic, HIV and mental health records, each one category. No general medical records right found. Level 1 stands. Add pending true for P.A. 104-471, effective 2027-07-01.
problems: pending is false, but P.A. 104-471 Section 20 creates a right to sue electronic health networks, effective 2027-07-01. It must be listed with pending true.
740 ILCS 110/15 (mental health records right to sue) is named in the note but not listed in provisions.
